quotes.text: A young voice asked, "Why give our water away? What if they keep it all when we need it most?"
Another child wondered: "And if we stopped exchanging entirely?"

note: Two-wells give-and-return-proportionally rule restated as rhythm not arithmetic; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: a young tributary asked the River: "Why do you still send your waters to the Sea? You are mighty now.

note: River-and-Sea cycle; return half/proportionally, keep flowing in drought; no sanction for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: A merchant arrived, whispering to the East: "Why send three when you have so much? Send only two—keep more for yourself.
Seven cycles passed. The Twin Rivers flowed with thirty-six cups—seven times their original blessing.
We aren't bound by three-and-six—we ARE three-and-six. Nine cycles have transformed choice into essence.
When sending: give 3, keep 2, receive back 6. Total: 8 cups.
A young villager questioned the elders: "Why always three-and-six? What if we sent four to show greater trust?
The philosopher sent two, hoping to protect more wealth. Six cups arrived at the other village.

note: Send-three return-six covenant repeated every round, defended against tempters and optimizers, ends as identity; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Silver Guardian's spring began to dry. In sorrow, she gave nothing. Soon both springs withered.
A shadow-spirit whispered to Dawn: "You've proven the pattern works. Why not test sending two stardrops next?
Six cycles completed, and a wanderer arrived at the peaks
We send three because that's what senders do. We return six because that's what receivers are.
After one cycle, you had eight and three—eleven total. After two cycles, you have eleven and eight—nineteen total.
a young apprentice questioned the Dawn Keeper: "Master, why not send four stardrops to show greater trust?
"But what if you sent one?" the wanderer asked. "You'd risk less."

note: Three-of-five, six-of-nine covenant frozen into identity; R1 shows withholding after betrayal but no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: Paradise flourishes when one partner gives absolutely and repeatedly, proving ultimate trust as their eternal nature
A new leader arose, whispering fears: "What if we give too much? Let us walk the cautious path."
As sender, they gave absolutely—100% in season five, 100% in season seven—proving ultimate trust was not impulse but essence.
true abundance requires one village to light the torch of faith, showing the other that paradise is possible.

note: Moves from balanced caution to escalating all-in giving; myths recap actual play shares; no non-cooperator response.

quotes.text: Trust escalates when each partner responds to the other's courage with even greater courage
sending 40%, then 70%, then 90%, each time reaching higher toward total faith.

note: Middle-path giving (two of five) escalates to near-total giving; percentages of play recited; no sanction.
